utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. It is a pleasure to see you at a distance. May I remind you, sir, that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Now Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We'll take that as a compliment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is intended to reflect upon the cosiness of our normal courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, I'm not going to explore with you further the extent of the injuries you that you observed on Atulla Qaili when you interviewed him on the night of 12th, 13th August. However, I do want to explore with you another aspect of Mr. Qaili's case that Ms. Residovic raised with you yesterday. At page 4376 of the transcript, Ms. Residovic explained to you that, according to one witness, police officers came twice to the home of the brother of Mr. Atulla Qaili, and Ms. Residovic asked you: "Would that indicate that probably your colleagues from other departments were trying to learn a bit more about the actual death of Atulla Qaili." And you responded: "Yes, yes. It is correct. Other colleagues and also us from the operative department in the Cair police station repeatedly tried to gather information not only on Atulla but also on the other persons, but the route to cooperation was closed by the villagers so we had no opportunity to get at any information." Do you recall that exchange yesterday with my colleague Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Help us please understand something, Mr. Toskovski. How would the police have located the brother of Atulla Qaili and the brother's address?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you please clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, yesterday Ms. Residovic told you that police officers went to the home of the brother of Atulla Qaili to ask him some questions. And so I'm asking you how the police would have found the brother, where would they have gone to look for an address, how would they have learned that Mr. Qaili had a brother. Where does this information come from?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this concrete case, but from various sources such information can be obtained. In this concrete case, I do not know from where the police obtained this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, more specifically what you mean by "various sources"? What kinds of sources, which sources?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are, above all, the official records, then friends in the village or in the city, and similar sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say the "official records," again, please, just so that we understand you, can you be more specific? What kind of official records?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's an ID database with information about all persons of age who hold an ID in the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so as part of a police investigation they would look at such databases. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Toskovski, which of your colleagues went to the house of Atulla Qaili's brother?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which colleagues went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know the specific reasons why your colleagues went to the home of Atulla Qaili's brother?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the concrete reasons, but I presume that this was about what we talked about earlier, to obtain some information in regards to the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know the results of the visit? Do you know what was said between your colleagues and Atulla Qaili's brother?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this report, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. You talked about how police repeatedly tried to gather information about Atulla Qaili during this time. Did the police check the medical records for Atulla Qaili at Skopje City Hospital, or speak with the doctors who treated Mr. Qaili there?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if this had happened, would you have received the information to include it in your report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that this would have been so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know whether the police reviewed the autopsy report for Atulla Qaili? An autopsy was performed on him -- I can't be specific, it was either the 13th or the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police does not look at these results. These result from the autopsy are submitted to the public prosecutor and the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, could the police speak with the doctors at the Forensic Institute in Skopje who performed the autopsy?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know, but I presume that for the unit for violent crimes spoke with him about this. He should have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if that was done, where would the record of such a discussion be, where would we find that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the analytics sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to come back to the analytics sector in a moment. Yesterday at page 4368, you explained to my colleague that when you submitted your criminal report about the ten arrested persons who were being detained at Mirkovci police station, you were still waiting for the results of paraffin glove tests to arrive. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall the results of these paraffin glove tests for those ten persons who were detained at Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, what is Exhibit P46, page 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 14th of August, 2001. It's sent to the SOI, Skopje, OKT. Can you tell us, Mr. Toskovski, what these abbreviations mean, SOI Skopje, OKT?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: SVR sector for criminal techniques.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The subject is analysis of fire-arm residues related to your act dated 12 August 2001. And this document from an expert named Silvija Kunovska and the head officer, Miroslav Uslinkovski. Says that "Regarding your letter, where you are looking for information whether there's a presence of a gunpowder residue on the delivered pieces of foils related to the withdrawn tests on the hands of the follows persons," and then we see the names of the ten persons who were detained at Mirkovci, "We would like to inform you that because of the existence of an immense contamination (dirtiness of various natures) found at the delivered foils, we are not able to perform the examination you have requested. Actually, we cannot apply any proper methods in order to find out, that is, detect whether there is presence of gunpowder particle on the hands of the accused." Can we agree, Mr. Toskovski, that, actually, there were no test results confirming the presence of nitrates on the hands of the ten persons who were detained at Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with this. I received oral information that most of the tests tested positive. I don't know whether all of these persons are those from the criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: These persons are the persons that are on the criminal report that you at least began to draft on the 13th of August, persons who you interviewed at Mirkovci police station on the night of 12 and 13 August.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were additional investigations and that there was a positive paraffin glove test.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where would such a positive result be located?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were submitted to the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. At page 4386, yesterday you explained to Ms. Residovic that between the 12th and 31st of August when you submitted your report about the events in Ljuboten you and your colleagues were constantly trying to find more information about what happened at Ljuboten. My question for you is this: Do you recall whether you reviewed the daily log-books of the Cair and Mirkovci police station to see if the log-books might provide you with additional information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The daily log-book in Mirkovci I have seen this one to see whether such persons were registered, the persons that were detained in Mirkovci were registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you review this log-book to give you any indication of which members of the Macedonian police might have been in Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen such an information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you spoke with your superior, Ljube Krstevski, about finding information about which police officers were in Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have such a conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Dragan Jakimovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know such a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yesterday at page 4387 you told Ms. Residovic that you reviewed the information that came into the analytical sector at Cair police station with respect to the events in Ljuboten. Help us understanding something, sir. After information comes into the analytical sector at Cair police station, where does that analytical sector send the information? Where does it go from Cair?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such information go to the analytical centre of SVR Skopje, of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then from there, where would that information go?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the analytical centre of the Ministry of Interior, on the level of the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. And that would be in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the city?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at the level of the state, does the analytical sector maintain an archive for all this information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, when the state, the sector for analytics at the state level receives all this information, does that department, that unit, keep the information in some form, in some place?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know their technology of work. I presume that this would be so, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After you finished interviewing the ten arrested persons on the night of 12 to 13 August, about what time did you leave the Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning of the 13th? Around 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yesterday at page 4374 of the transcript you told my learned colleague that if an investigative judge had information about mistreatment of a detainee they would have undertaken an investigation. Let me ask you this: Suppose an investigating judge had information indicating that detainees might have been mistreated but did not investigate further. What conclusion would you draw from that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not comment the work of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you will be pleased to know that that concludes the questions to be asked of you. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance here in The Hague and the assistance you have been able to give and the court officer will show you out. Thank you, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And would you bring in the next witness. Mr. Dobbyn, good morning. The name of your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning. Is Ejup Hamiti, H-a-m-i-t-i, formerly known as Ejup Ametov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that has been given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Now Mr. Dobbyn has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hamiti.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hamiti, do you recall giving a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on 9 February 2003?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall that on 19 November 2005 the statement was certified by an officer of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At that time, did you have an opportunity to read the statement in your native language?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to make any corrections and additions to that statement?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Were those corrections and additions handwritten into your statement and also included in an addendum to the statement?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that the content of your statement with these corrections and the addendum is accurate and correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would seek to tender the statement and the addendum which bears the ERN N002-1977 N002-1987, pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Simply to have a clarification from Mr. Dobbyn on this point. We had understood in the past that the Prosecution would not seek to tender the comments made by the witness in relation to particular documents and in this particular case it would seem that the comments are attached to the addendum, so if Mr. Dobbyn could simply indicate that, in fact, they only seek to tender the clarification and correction made by the witness as opposed to the comments which he made about certain documents, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the addendum I am referring to does not contain any comments to documents. The ERN of that particular addendum is N002-1985 to N002-1986. It was made on 19 November 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the Prosecutor, Your Honour. We have a different version, whether to connect it together. We're grateful, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The statement with the addendum will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P417, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at this time with Your Honour's permission I will read a summary of that particular statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The witness, Ejup Hamiti, formerly known as Ejup Ametov is a Ljuboten resident of Albanian ethnicity. Between 10 and 12 August 2001 Ljuboten was targeted with gun-fire and shelling. On 12 August the witness saw a neighbour's house and barn burning and a neighbour himself injured during attack. The witness took cover by a river, along with a large number of other villagers. The witness intended to return to the village but was informed that the police had entered Ljuboten and that it was unsafe to return. The witness then joined other villagers fleeing towards Skopje. As they approached a check-point on the road to Skopje, the witness and others were approached by a policeman who abused them and then signalled a number of Macedonian civilians who were gathered in the area to beat the witness and other Ljuboten villagers. The witness and another villager, Dilaver Fetahovski, started running away towards Radisani. Two policemen ordered them to stop before opening fire on them. The witness was hit in the forehead by a bullet and fell unconscious. The witness was subsequently admitted to intensive care at Skopje City Hospital where he under went emergency surgery. Once he regained consciousness his legs and hands were tied as were those of the other Ljuboten villagers he saw at the hospital. The witness was released from hospital on 17 August 2001 but continues to suffer health problems as a result of his head injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, at this point Mr. Hamiti, I'm going to be asking you a few questions and I would just ask that you listen very carefully to the question and provide an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would like to call 65 ter number 199.21. This is a photograph which is also on page 15 of the court binder. And, I'm sorry, before I forget, Your Honours, we have prepared witness binders for Your Honours and also for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Hamiti, in your statement you describe being beaten by Macedonian civilians at a location near a police check-point on the way to Skopje. On the photograph which is on the screen in front of you, can you see where that check-point was located?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes. Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could I ask for the usher's assistance at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Hamiti, with the assistance of the usher, would you be able to draw a circle in the area where that check-point was located?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you draw the number 1 above that circle, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Inside or outside the circle?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Outside the circle, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And on this photograph, can you locate an area known as Buzalak?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes. Buzalak of Ljuboten is here approximately; and down here you have Buzalak of Radisani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you draw circles around those locations, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I see you have drawn two circles. The one on the left, what is the name of that area?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Buzalak of Radisani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you put the number 2 above that, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the area to the right, what is that known as?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Buzalak of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you put the number 3 above that, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And on this photograph, are you able to see a location known as Kodra e Zajmit?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: In relation to this photograph, can you tell us where Kodra e Zajmit is located?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Kodra e Zajmit is on the left side of this road, 200 to 300 metres on the left side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you draw an arrow in the direction of Kodra e Zajmit, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you put the number 4 above that.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, that in relation to this photograph, which direction is Skopje?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Behind the arrow which is on the road under number 4, this is the road taking to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And on this photograph, can you see the location where you, your friend Dilaver Fetahovski and his father were beaten by the Macedonian civilians?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: No. It's more in the inside, here approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So am I correct in understanding that it's very close to that location but not actually visible in the photo?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes. It's nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put the number 5 above that circle, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn, as I've understood the evidence, both the markings 2 and 3 are of Buzalak of Radisani. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honour, was that number 2 is Buzalak of Radisani; number 3 is Buzalak of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If I could just clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Hamiti?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P418, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Hamiti, the policeman who signalled to the civilians to beat you that you described in your statement, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you describe that uniform?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Approximately, I don't remember very well, when I saw beating them -- when started beating them, I lost my consciousness. I only saw that they were wearing police uniforms. They had the patch writing police. Afterwards, they started beating us, and this is it. Like this uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, could you please not look at that photograph just yet, Mr. Hamiti. We'll be coming to that at a certain time.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, at this time I would like to call up Exhibit P00015. This is also photograph A from page 23 of the Prosecution's Court binder. And it is in tab 2 of this witness binder. If could you please look at tab 2 of the binder, Mr. Hamiti. Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes. They wore these kind of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, apart from the policeman who signalled to the Macedonian civilians to beat you, did you see any other policemen that day, the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes, we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And where did you see these other policemen?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: While running towards Radisani I saw two policeman. Then I lost my consciousness when I was hit by the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. What were those policemen wearing?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: They were too far away. I just could see that they were policemen. They had automatic rifles as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Before the 12th of August, 2001, had you passed through any check-points around the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes. We regularly went through the check-point I signalled there. I was a student and I had to go regularly through that check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what uniforms, if any, did the policemen at these check-points wear?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: This kind of uniforms, the uniforms that are on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honours, I would like to show a video-clip. This 65 ter number 309, the ERN is V000-3494. The clip I would like to show starts at 1 minute 50 seconds and runs until 2 minutes 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Hamiti, I would ask to you look very carefully at the screen. A video-clip will be coming up and I would ask to you watch that very carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Hamiti, do you know which date this video recording was made?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: The day the events occurred, on August the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what does this video show?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: The video shows us running away. Then it shows when they fired upon us and when I was hit and when I fell down. The video shows this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You say that "the video shows us running away." Who is the other individual who's running down the hill with you?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Dilaver Fetahovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not there video has been shown on Macedonian television?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would seek to tender this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P419, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Hamiti, in the Albanian language version of your state it says that you were shot on the right side of your forehead, while in the English language version it says you were shot on the left side of your forehead. Could you clarify this and tell us what side of the forehead the bullet hit?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: The left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hamiti, could I ask you to lift up the fringe of your hair. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for the record I'd ask it to reflect that is shown the witness has lifted his hair, revealing a, for want of a better word, a crater on the left side of his forehead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, the injury that you've just shown us, Mr. Hamiti, was this caused by the bullet that struck you on 12th August 2001?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: In your state you describe after being hit by the bullet falling unconscious and then when regaining consciousness finding yourself in Skopje City Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at this time, I would like to call up exhibit P 00192 and I'd like to see page 6 of this exhibit which is ERN N000-5719. And there is also in tab 4 of the witness binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So if you would like to look at the document in tab 4, Mr. Hamiti.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: This is a medical report from Skopje City Hospital. Mr. Hamiti, do you see your name on the upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the first line states: "On 12 August 2001 Ejup Ametov was admitted to the clinic as an urgent case with a head and brain injury caused by a projectile." Is this an accurate description of when you were admitted to the hospital and the reason for your admission?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in your statement and in the addendum to your statement you have described the health problems that you have suffered as a result of your head injury. You've stated that you faint every now and then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I didn't mean to interrupt the question but it seems that the document is not the correct document on the screen. I simply wanted to indicate that to my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you for pointing that out, Mr. Mettraux. I was actually looking at the document I had in tab 4. Thank you. I believe we need page 6 to be shown on the screen, page 6 of that particular exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This exhibit has only one page, Mr. Dobbyn. You may have a wrong number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I understand it's my fault. I asked for Exhibit P192 to be shown. I should have been asking for P220. I apologise. As the witness has spoken to that document, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Hamiti, you have stated that you faint every now and then. Do you have a medical diagnosis for this condition?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes. After the injury, I got epilepsy and I go regularly to medical checks every second or third month. And I pay all the bills myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Have you been told whether or not your epilepsy is related to your head injury?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes, I have. It was caused by the injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Since the 12th of August, 2001 until today, have you ever been contacted by anyone from the Macedonian police or the Macedonian government and asked about what happened to you and what took place in Ljuboten on 10 to 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Have you taken any steps yourself against the Macedonian police or the Macedonian government to have someone held accountable for what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you please explain what you have done.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I have taken the state to court, because injustice was inflicted to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: By saying you have taken the state to court, could you explain further?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I filed charges against the state because on the photograph it can be clearly seen that I was a civilian, and the documents, all the documents of it, I have taken also from the hospital, everything comes up very clearly and have I filed charges against them, and it is in judicial procedure now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I have no further questions at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn, the document on the screen, I'm told is not an exhibit. It's part of the 65 ter Exhibit 220. Do you want it to become an exhibit in the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I apologise, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Just this one page?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P420, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dobbyn. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hamiti. My name is Guenael Mettraux and together with my colleague Edina Residovic I'm appearing on behalf of Mr. Boskoski. Mr. Hamiti, we have been given a copy of your statement already and I do not wish to go over the entirety of the information which you have provided to the Prosecution and the Court. There is a number of matter which I would like to clarify about the circumstances in which you received this grave wound. Am I correct to understand that because of the circumstances at the time, the fear and also the commotion around you, you were in a great of stress. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: When arrived at the check-point, I saw these civilians and when I saw them beating the people with -- together with the policemen, this is why I started running. I started running towards Radisani, but instead of going -- of taking the road, I went to Radisani. When I started running, I didn't know where I was going. This is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct as you were running your friend Dilaver Fetahovski was a few metres behind you, 20 or so metres behind you?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: As I told you, I was very confused. I don't know whether Dilaver was behind me. I can only speak of myself. I started running. I couldn't even see whether there was someone running behind me. I don't know how much you can understand me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct because of the state of excitement you were not able at the time to see where the shot had come from, the shot that hit you?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. When I saw Dilaver being beaten up and his father being beaten up, I was very frightened and confused. I started running. I saw two policemen from my left side. When they started shooting, I just heard the shot from automatic rifles. I couldn't hear the bullet that hit me. I just fell on the ground and for two hours I stayed there in this -- in this situation of coma.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And these two policemen which you have just indicated, those are the same policemen as you had mentioned to the Prosecution when you gave your statement on the 9th of February of 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your statement, I believe you have indicated that those people who you believe to be policemen were about 50 metres or so away from you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Approximately. As I told you, I cannot be precise. It was approximately 50 metres. As I told you, I was very confused. I could only see that they were policemen and they were carrying automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I suppose that you will agree with me that Dilaver was running behind you would also have been in a position to see these two men. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Sir, I was telling you about myself. I couldn't see Dilaver and I was in a state of coma for two hours. I'm describing to you my state. And then the ambulance came and took me to the hospital in the town and I was -- and I underwent an urgent surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I can ask it to you that way. Was there any impediment or any reason why Dilaver would not have seen these two policemen, in so far as can you say?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I apologise, but I cannot speak in Dilaver's name. I can only speak in my own name and describe to you my state and what I went through. If you have questions for him, maybe it's better to ask him directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that the reason you believed that these two men were police officers were because of their uniforms, the uniforms they were wearing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: You could see their uniforms very well. And I saw them with automatic rifles. I don't know how clear I am, but they had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that on that day you've indicated to the Prosecution that you only saw one man wearing what you believe to be a police patch and that was in the vicinity of the check-point? Is that what you told the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I will explain in detail. This one policeman, this is the one who took us from Buzalak of Radisani up to the Macedonian civilians. This is the one -- when we were running in the direction of Radisani, these two persons were other policemen, not the same with the one I mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, that this is the way the matter was understood as well. Is that correct then that you have indicated to the Prosecution that you only saw one man wearing a patch which you identified as a police patch or police insignia and that was in the vicinity of the check-point? In other words, you did not identify any patches or insignia on the two other policemen which were by your side as you were running. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: They were far, but I saw them carrying automatic rifle, and you can tell police uniforms. The police that was with us at Buzalak of Radisani, he was there and he was also wearing automatic rifle, but his patch, I could see, and "policija" was written on his patch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that you were interviewed by representative of the Prosecution earlier that year in June, in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall the representative of the Prosecution showing you a number of pictures during that interview?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that one of the pictures that were shown to you were pictures of patches, police patches. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall saying this to the Prosecution upon being shown those pictures: "I can see these are police patches but I cannot be certain that these are the same as the patch I saw on the policeman uniform on the day I was shot." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Just a moment, sir. These two policemen that I mentioned, they were far, quite far, 50 to 100 metres far, and I could not see their uniforms clearly, but the policeman who was with us previously, he was very near, and I could see his patch and what was written on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, sir, that in fact are you not certain whether the two men who you saw by your side were policemen or members of the Macedonian army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I couldn't tell whether they were soldiers or policemen, but they were wearing uniforms and I described you my state of mind when I started running. I was completely confused and out of myself and I couldn't tell clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you know a person named Saqir Fetahovski, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Fetahovski is a fellow villager. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on that day he was also present with you near to the check-points which you have indicated earlier today. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he would have also seen you run away from this check-point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I don't know. Ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If Mr. Fetahovski were to say that the people whom you saw shoot in your directions were soldiers and not police officers, you would have no reason to disbelieve him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I told you that I wasn't quite conscious about my deeds. I could only see them wearing uniforms, police uniforms. Maybe he was in position to see them better than me, but I doubt, because he was quite severely beaten too.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, however, that are you not certain that the shot that hit you had in fact come from either of these two men. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I don't know precisely who fired, but I could hear the sound of the shot. I don't know how clear I am. I could hear the shot coming from the automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you are not certain that the shot in question came from either of those two persons. You did not have the time to look whether it could have came from elsewhere. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think in that case, I have no further question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm grateful to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Antonio Apostolski, and with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, I appear for Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Is it correct that you completed your primary education in your own village, Ljuboten, and in your mother tongue, in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: After that you completed your secondary education in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you gave your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you were a student at the pedagogy faculty in Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please tell me when did you enrol in this faculty?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes. I enrolled in the academic year 2000/2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you carried out your studies in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you passed by several check-points. Is it correct that there was a check-point on the last bus-stop of bus number 57 in Radisani neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, but I'm not speaking about Radisani. I'm talking here about the road that links Ljuboten and Skopje. On this road, there was only one check-point and this check-point was located at Cezma e Rizvanit, and you may very well now about this location because this check-point was set up well ahead before the Ljuboten events.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about your statement but in general, considering the fact that you travelled a lot in that region, is it correct that there was a check-point at the last bus-stop of bus number 57 at Radisani neighbourhood? Are you familiar with this fact?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: I went by car through our road. I didn't travel on bus and that's why I am not familiar where this check-point was. I'm not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking in general terms, not about the concrete dates. I'm asking you about the whole period, July, August, since you travelled frequently from Ljuboten to Skopje. During this period of time, did you see this check-point?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: And I think I'm explaining it very well. Maybe you are familiar with the road that links Ljuboten and Skopje, not the road, the old road that links Ljuboten with Skopje through Ljubanci. And this was the only check-point that I saw on that road, and we regularly passed by this check-point. I never went to Radishan and I always travelled by car. I don't know how clear I am, and I'm speaking about the year 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Hamiti, you described the check-point on the road between Ljuboten and Skopje. And what name did you refer to that check-point by?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: We used to call the check-point Cezma e Rizvanit. There is a water fountain nearby called Cezma e Rizvanit. And that's how we called this check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is this the same check-point that was in the photo earlier that you were approaching on the 12th of August when you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So am I correct in my understanding that this check-point is located in an area which is between Buzalak and between Kodra e Zajmit?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you also described earlier that you passed through this check-point on several occasions before the 12th of August as you travelled to Skopje for school.

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: Yes, I was a student, and I regularly attended school.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Lectures, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: On these occasions when you passed through the check-point, who manned the check-point? Was it police or was it army?

utterances.speaker: EJUP HAMITI
utterances.text: The police. The police and reservists that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you for your time, Mr. Hamiti.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dobbyn. You will be pleased to know, Mr. Hamiti, that that concludes the questions that will be asked of you. The Chamber is very grateful indeed for your assistance, for the trouble you've been to come here and give evidence, and you are now, of course, able to leave and return to your home and normal activities. We will be adjourning shortly and then the court officer will show you out. So thank you, indeed. If there is no other matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon is standing with purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The only purpose, Your Honour, is to simply confirm that the Prosecution did not anticipate that this witness would go so quickly and therefore we do not have another witness to call this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We anticipated that from what you had said, Mr. Saxon, and we therefore continue on Monday. The Monday session, I believe, has been moved to the afternoon at 2.15, in case everybody had not caught up with that. So we adjourn now and resume on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.17 a.m.,
